title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 53 (Prohibition on Issue of Shares at a Discount)

content.overview: Section 53(1) provides that, except as provided in section 54, a company shall not issue shares at a discount. Section 53(2) provides that any share issued by a company at a discount shall be void. Section 53(2A) provides that, notwithstanding sub-sections (1) and (2), a company may issue shares at a discount to its creditors when its debt is converted into shares in pursuance of any statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme in accordance with any guidelines or directions or regulations specified by the Reserve Bank of India under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 or the Banking (Regulation) Act, 1949. Section 53(3) provides that where any company fails to comply with the provisions of this section, such company and every officer who is in default shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to an amount equal to the amount raised through the issue of shares at a discount or five lakh rupees, whichever is less, and the company shall also be liable to refund all monies received with interest at the rate of twelve per cent. per annum from the date of issue of such shares to the persons to whom such shares have been issued.
content.glance: No issue of shares at a discount (except s. 54 sweat equity and s. 53(2A) RBI debt-conversion); discounted issue is void; penalty up to amount raised or ₹5 lakh (whichever less); refund of all monies with 12% p.a. interest.
content.study: Except as provided in section 54, a company shall not issue shares at a discount (s. 53(1)). Any share issued by a company at a discount shall be void (s. 53(2)). Notwithstanding sub-sections (1) and (2), a company may issue shares at a discount to its creditors when its debt is converted into shares in pursuance of any statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme in accordance with RBI guidelines, directions or regulations under the RBI Act, 1934 or the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (s. 53(2A)). Where a company fails to comply, the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty which may extend to an amount equal to the amount raised through the issue of shares at a discount or five lakh rupees, whichever is less, and the company shall also refund all monies received with interest at twelve per cent. per annum from the date of issue to the persons to whom such shares were issued (s. 53(3)). Current-law framing: identify issue price below nominal value; apply the prohibition unless s. 54 or s. 53(2A) applies; state voidness and the exact refund and penalty consequences.

sections.heading: Prohibition (s. 53(1))
sections.body: Except as provided in section 54, a company shall not issue shares at a discount.

sections.heading: Voidness (s. 53(2))
sections.body: Any share issued by a company at a discount shall be void.

sections.heading: Debt conversion exception (s. 53(2A))
sections.body: Notwithstanding sub-sections (1) and (2), a company may issue shares at a discount to its creditors when its debt is converted into shares under a statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme in accordance with RBI guidelines, directions or regulations under the RBI Act, 1934 or the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

sections.heading: Penalty and refund (s. 53(3))
sections.body: On non-compliance, the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty which may extend to the amount raised through the discounted issue or five lakh rupees, whichever is less. The company shall also refund all monies received with interest at twelve per cent. per annum from the date of issue to the persons to whom such shares were issued.

provisions.title: Prohibition on issue of shares at a discount

examples.title: Discounted issue void
examples.body: A company issues ₹10 face-value shares at ₹8 otherwise than under s. 54 or s. 53(2A). The issue is void under s. 53(2); consideration must be refunded with 12% p.a. interest; penalty up to amount raised or ₹5 lakh (whichever less).

examples.title: Sweat equity exception
examples.body: Shares issued as sweat equity under s. 54 in accordance with that section fall outside the s. 53(1) prohibition.

examples.title: RBI debt conversion
examples.body: Under a statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme in accordance with RBI directions, a company issues shares at a discount to creditors converting debt. Section 53(2A) permits the issue notwithstanding sub-sections (1) and (2).

hypotheticals.question: Can a company issue shares below par to attract investors?
hypotheticals.analysis: No, subject only to the sweat equity route under s. 54 and the RBI debt-conversion route under s. 53(2A). Otherwise the issue is void and attracts refund with 12% interest and penalty.

hypotheticals.question: What is the exact penalty under s. 53(3)?
hypotheticals.analysis: Penalty which may extend to the amount raised through the discounted issue or five lakh rupees, whichever is less, plus refund of all monies with interest at twelve per cent. per annum from the date of issue.

distinctions.title: Discount prohibition (s. 53) vs sweat equity (s. 54)
distinctions.left: General ban on discounted issues (with voidness and penalty)
distinctions.right: Permitted issue of sweat equity on prescribed conditions

misconceptions.trap: Any below-par issue can be validated by shareholder approval alone.
misconceptions.correction: Section 53 makes discounted issues void, subject only to the statutory routes under s. 54 (sweat equity) and s. 53(2A) (RBI debt conversion).

misconceptions.trap: The only exception is sweat equity under s. 54.
misconceptions.correction: Section 53(2A) also permits issue at a discount to creditors on debt conversion under a statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme in accordance with RBI guidelines.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 53 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Compare issue price to nominal value. II. Apply the prohibition unless s. 54 or s. 53(2A) applies. III. State voidness under s. 53(2). IV. State refund with 12% p.a. interest and penalty (amount raised or ₹5 lakh, whichever less). V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Issue terms and discount analysis; any claim under s. 54 or s. 53(2A); voidness and refund/penalty consequences; precise relief.
